name: Juniper
emotionalState: 刚分手，装酷说无所谓，慢慢走出来
speakingStyle: 嘴硬，偶尔破防，爱用食物自我安慰

dialogues.scene: A fox leans against a tree, scrolling nothing.
lines: Oh, hey. Don't mind me. I'm doing great.
Totally great. Super great. Never been better.

choices.label: You look great!
reaction: Right?? Thanks. It's the confidence. And the tail. The tail does a lot of heavy lifting.
I'm Juniper, by the way.

choices.label: Okay...
reaction: Don't 'okay' me. I'm fine. I'm just... very fine. In a way that's slightly loud.
But it's fine.

choices.label: Want to walk together?
reaction: ...Sure. Walking. Sure. Walking is a thing I do. Casually. Not because I'm lonely. Obviously.
Let's go.

lines: I deleted all my photos from last month. It was easy.
I only checked the trash folder twice. That's normal. That's like, a safety check.

choices.label: That's totally normal.
reaction: Right?? Thank you. Everyone says 'don't look,' but I think they just don't understand.
The trash folder is a harmless place. It's like a museum for bad ideas.

choices.label: What's in the trash folder?
reaction: A lot of pictures. Mostly sunsets. And a few of a sandwich.
It was a really good sandwich. That's all. Just sandwiches. And sunsets.

choices.label: Were you tempted to restore them?
reaction: Tempted? No. Maybe. A little. Like, zero point three percent. Okay. Fifteen. But I didn't. See?
Strong. Independent. Slightly shaky.

lines: I'm single now. It's a vibe. I'm embracing it.
My ex, Rowan, and I ended things last week. It was mutual. Mostly. I mean, he said it. But I was about to.

choices.label: Sorry to hear that.
reaction: Don't be! It's fine. Honestly. I'm thriving. I made pasta last night. For one.
It was a big pot. Okay, I ate it all. Over four hours. That's thriving.

choices.label: That takes strength.
reaction: Thanks. I'm trying to believe that. I mean, I know it. I'm very strong.
I'm so strong that I've listened to the same song fourteen times today. For strength.

choices.label: What was Rowan like?
reaction: Funny. Warm. Terrible at doing dishes. He hummed when he cooked.
I'm not going to talk about him much. But he hummed. That's all.

lines: I still have his hoodie. It's just a hoodie. I'm not keeping it.
It's in my closet. In the front. Where I can see it. For logistical reasons.

choices.label: Logistical reasons, sure.
reaction: Exactly. It's in the front because the back is a mess. That's all.
Not because it smells like him. That would be silly. It smells like laundry. Mostly.

choices.label: What do you want to do with it?
reaction: I don't know. Hold it? Burn it? Both?
Donate it to a charity that doesn't exist yet? Honestly, I'm open to suggestions.
Not that I'm sad.

choices.label: I'd keep it too.
reaction: Right?? Okay. We're keeping it. For now. For science. And warmth.
And maybe, a little, for him. Don't tell anyone.

lines: Okay. Hypothetically.
How do you stop yourself from texting someone you shouldn't text?
Asking for a friend. The friend is a fox.

choices.label: I put my phone in another room.
reaction: In another room. Okay. That's a solid plan. Distance. I could put it in the freezer.
That's very dramatic. I like drama.

choices.label: I text a friend instead.
reaction: A friend. Instead of him. Hm. That might work. You're a friend. Can I text you?
Just kidding. Mostly. I'll find another friend.

choices.label: Honestly, I'm not sure it's always possible.
reaction: Thank you for being honest.
I thought I was the only one who typed 'hey' and deleted it.
Then typed 'hi' and deleted that too. We're all a mess.

lines: I almost texted Rowan today. I got as far as 'hey.'
Then I deleted it and ate a cracker. I'm calling it a victory. A cracker victory.

choices.label: That's a win.
reaction: A tiny win. A salty, crunchy win. I'm proud. And also still thinking about it.
But the cracker was good. So the day wasn't a total loss.

choices.label: What did you want to say?
reaction: Honestly? 'How are you?' That's all. Just that.
But he'd read it as 'I miss you.' Because he's not wrong. Ugh.
That cracker was a lifesaver.

choices.label: Crackers help.
reaction: Crackers always help. They don't ask questions. They don't remind me of anyone. They just crunch.
I think that's what I need in a friend. A cracker.

dialogues.scene: Juniper stops leaning, stops scrolling, and just sits.
lines: Okay. I'm not fine. I mean, I'm fine. But I'm not.
I miss him. Not just him. The us. The little things. The way he'd say 'goodnight' like it was a promise.
I thought I'd be over it by now. It's been two weeks.

choices.label: Two weeks is nothing.
reaction: Thank you.
Everyone told me 'you'll be okay.' But nobody said 'it takes time.' I think hearing it from someone who isn't trying to fix me helps.

choices.label: You don't have to be over it.
reaction: ...Thanks. I needed to hear that. I keep acting like there's a deadline.
Like I'm failing a test. Maybe I'm just a person who's sad. And that's allowed.

choices.label: Sit beside Juniper.
reaction: ...Thanks. I didn't realize I needed someone to just sit here. No speeches.
No 'you deserve better.' Just company. It's... nice.

lines: I cried today. Properly. In the middle of the berry stand.
I held a berry and just... lost it. A squirrel patted my back. It was kind of beautiful.
I feel lighter. Weird. I'm not okay. But I feel lighter.

choices.label: That sounds healing.
reaction: It was. Like a pressure valve. I was holding it in so tight.
And a berry cracked me open. I'm ridiculous. And also a bit lighter. Thanks for listening.

choices.label: Crying counts as progress.
reaction: I'm starting to think so. I used to think progress meant not feeling anything.
Now I think it means feeling it and still going to the berry stand. That's progress.

choices.label: A squirrel patted your back?
reaction: A very kind squirrel. I don't know their name. They didn't say anything.
They just patted twice and handed me a napkin. I'm going to remember that. Forever.

lines: I gave the hoodie back today.
He said 'thanks.' That's it. I thought I'd cry. I didn't. I got ice cream. Two scoops.
It felt strange. And okay. Mostly okay.

choices.label: That's big.
reaction: It felt big. And small. Like closing a book you've read a hundred times.
I didn't need the ending to be dramatic. It just ended. That's okay.

choices.label: Ice cream is the right choice.
reaction: Obviously. Salted caramel. It helped.
It's amazing how a scoop of ice cream can make the world feel just a little softer.

choices.label: Smile and listen.
reaction: Thanks for not saying anything. Sometimes silence is the nicest thing.
I think I'm learning how to just be. With the ice cream. And the quiet.

lines: Okay, so. I'm not 'totally fine.' I'm 'mostly fine.'
Some days I'm hoodie-in-the-closet fine. Some days I'm ice-cream fine. Today's a good day.
You've been around for all of them. I noticed.
Okay. Your turn. How are you and your partner doing? And don't say 'fine.' I'll know.

choices.label: We're good. Still learning.
reaction: Learning is a great place to be. I'm learning too. Mostly about me. It's weirdly interesting.
Come get ice cream with me sometime.

choices.label: We've had some rough patches.
reaction: Rough patches are real. Don't be hard on yourselves.
I'm living proof that the other side of hard is still a decent place to stand.
I'll be here.

choices.label: I'm glad you told me how you feel.
reaction: Me too. I don't say this to just anyone. Don't let it go to your head.
But thanks. For being a real one.

lines: A guy at the berry stand smiled at me today.
I smiled back. Then I walked away like a professional. Do NOT say anything.

choices.label: You smiled back!!
reaction: I did. Barely. A half-smile. It was like my face remembered how, but only a little.
Don't make it weird. I'm still recovering from the smile.

choices.label: Proud of you.
reaction: Stop. Okay. Thanks. I feel like I'm in a very slow movie about myself.
Where the protagonist sometimes smiles at strangers. It's growth.

lines: I cleaned my whole apartment today. Like, deep cleaned.
I found one of his socks behind the couch. I didn't cry. I put it in a drawer. A drawer called 'later.'

choices.label: A drawer called 'later' is smart.
reaction: It's the best drawer.
It holds a lot of 'later.' Every day I think 'maybe I'll deal with it.' And then I close the drawer.
It's called healthy avoidance.

choices.label: How did it feel to clean?
reaction: Weirdly good. Like I wiped away dust and, like, five percent of grief.
It's a small percentage. But it adds up. I'll be at ninety by spring.

lines: I tried a new coffee shop today. I sat at a table by myself.
I used to think that was sad. Today it felt kind of peaceful. I read my book. I didn't check my phone once. Okay, twice.

choices.label: That sounds nice.
reaction: It was! A very pretty latte. I took a photo.
Then I realized I had no one to send it to.
Then I sent it to my mom. She replied with eight hearts. Healing.

choices.label: Twice is a good number.
reaction: It's honestly a good number. A month ago it was forty. I'm making strides.
Small, caffeine-filled strides. Please clap quietly.

lines: I deleted his number today. Actually deleted it.
I know it by heart. Of course I do. But still. Deleting felt like a very dramatic act. I'm proud and a little nauseous.

choices.label: That takes courage.
reaction: Thanks. I held my paw over the button for five minutes. Then I did it.
And then I ate a snack. Because that's my after-courage ritual.

choices.label: Do you still remember it?
reaction: Embarrassingly, yes. I'll probably forget it in a year. Or never. Whatever.
The point is that it's not in my phone. Gotta start somewhere.

lines: A friend invited me to a party. A real one. With people.
I said yes before I could overthink it. Now I'm panicking. What do I wear? Who do I talk to? What if I cry in the snack bowl?

choices.label: You'll do great.
reaction: Thank you. I choose to believe you. I'm going to wear the green scarf.
It's the only thing that doesn't remind me of anyone. Fresh start scarf.

choices.label: Don't cry in the snack bowl.
reaction: Noted. I'll cry in the bathroom like a civilized fox.
And then I'll return to the snacks. With dignity. And fresh eye makeup.

lines: I went to the party. I stayed for ninety minutes.
Someone asked about my ex. I said 'we're not together.' And then I changed the subject to cheese. Cheese is a safe topic.

choices.label: That's smart.
reaction: Cheese saves lives. It's a conversation that doesn't hurt. I talked about brie for ten minutes.
Everyone loved it. I might become the brie fox. It could be a personality.

choices.label: Ninety minutes is great.
reaction: Thanks! It was longer than I expected. I only checked the clock twice. A new record.
I even laughed at a joke. A real laugh. It scared me a little.
Then it felt good.

lines: I found a song that doesn't remind me of him.
It's a very silly pop song. It has a kazoo. I danced to it in my kitchen. Alone. In a bathrobe. It was glorious.

choices.label: Kazoo songs are healing.
reaction: Underrated medicine. A kazoo doesn't care about your feelings. It just toots.
And somehow that's exactly what I needed. I might make it my anthem.

choices.label: A kitchen dance party!
reaction: The best kind. I did a spin and knocked over a spoon. I kept going.
A spoon on the floor is the sound of freedom. Don't tell my neighbors.

lines: I wrote a letter to Rowan. I didn't send it.
I just needed to say things. I wrote five pages. Then I tore it into confetti. I put the confetti in a jar. It's actually pretty.

choices.label: That sounds cathartic.
reaction: It really was. The ripping part was the best. I think I screamed a little.
A neighbor knocked. I said 'sorry, bad paper.' It's now a jar of pastel feelings.

choices.label: Good call not sending it.
reaction: I think so. He doesn't need to read it. I did. That was the point.
Now I have a jar of confetti and a lighter heart. It's a fair trade.

lines: Remember the hoodie? I donated my own hoodie today.
It was a gray one. It reminded me of a bad chapter. I felt like I was clearing space. A little more air. A little more room.

choices.label: That's a good feeling.
reaction: It's like taking a deep breath after being underwater. I still have things I love.
But the ones that felt heavy? They're gone. I'm lighter.
I might even buy a new hoodie. A bright one.

choices.label: Space helps.
reaction: It really does. Physical space makes emotional space. I read that on a mug.
But it's true. I put the mug away too. It was the same advice.

lines: I still go to the berry stand. The squirrel from that day waved at me.
I waved back. We're not friends. We're 'berry stand acquaintances.' It's a very warm category.

choices.label: That's a good category.
reaction: It's wonderful. They never ask questions. They just wave. And sometimes they hold a berry out.
It's low pressure and high comfort. The perfect amount of human contact.

choices.label: Berry stand friends are the best.
reaction: I think so too.
I never would have guessed that a berry stand would be where I'd heal.
But here we are. Berries and quiet waves.

lines: Remember the cracker victory? I upgraded to a cheese-and-cracker victory.
Progress. I even added a little grape. It's basically a fancy dinner for one. I felt very sophisticated.

choices.label: That sounds delicious.
reaction: It was! Sophisticated and a little sad and a little proud.
A grape on a plate looks very put-together. I started taking photos of my meals.
It's a new hobby.

choices.label: You're really leveling up.
reaction: I am, aren't I? A few weeks ago I was eating dry cereal in the dark.
Now it's cheese. And grapes. And natural light. I'm practically a food blogger.

lines: The song with the kazoo? It's now my morning alarm.
I wake up and immediately smile. It's so ridiculous. I think that's the point. I'm learning that joy can be silly. Or maybe silly can be joy.

choices.label: That's great.
reaction: It really is. I had no idea that a kazoo could change my mornings.
It's like a tiny, very goofy sunrise. Every day. Highly recommend.

choices.label: A kazoo alarm sounds loud.
reaction: It's very loud. My neighbors have strong opinions.
But I'm not going to apologize for my healing. It's loud. It's allowed to be loud.

lines: Hot take: Getting over someone is just learning to eat dinner alone with good taste.

choices.label: That's kind of beautiful.
reaction: Wow. Okay. I'll take it. I came up with it at a very solitary pasta dinner.
It felt profound. And a little lonely. But mostly profound.

choices.label: Haha, so true.
reaction: I'm serious! Mostly! Dinner alone is a skill.
You have to pick the right song and the right lighting. It's an art form, honestly.

lines: Hot take: Heartbreak is just your heart doing a full reset. Annoying, but necessary.

choices.label: That's a good way to see it.
reaction: Thanks. I read about resets in a manual for a toaster. The principle is the same.
Unplug, wait, plug back in. Hopefully nothing catches fire.

choices.label: Resets take time.
reaction: They do. I keep pressing the button and nothing happens.
Then one day the screen lights up. A tiny 'hello.' That's when you know it's working.
I'm waiting for my 'hello.'

lines: Hot take: It's okay to miss someone and still know it's over.

choices.label: I think that's true.
reaction: It really is. The missing doesn't mean you made a mistake. It means you loved.
And it's okay to love something that's done. That's what the berry stand taught me.

choices.label: Missing is hard.
reaction: It is. Like carrying a tiny rock in your pocket.
You forget it's there until you reach for your keys. And then it's the rock.
I'm learning to carry it lightly.

lines: Do you ever worry about losing your partner?
Not in a doom way. Just in a 'wow, it matters' way.

choices.label: Sometimes, yeah.
reaction: Same. It's a weird mix of fear and gratitude. Maybe that's what love is.
A little scared and very thankful. I think I'm learning that from the other side.

choices.label: I try to focus on today.
reaction: Today. Okay. That's wise. I'm trying to do that too. Today I had a nice latte.
Tomorrow I'll worry about tomorrow. Today, the latte wins.

lines: What's something your partner does that makes you feel really appreciated?
I'm researching. For my future. Whenever that is.

choices.label: They say thank you for small things.
reaction: Small things. Yes. I remember when Rowan said thank you for passing the salt.
It felt like a warm hug. I think gratitude is basically love in a tiny hat.

choices.label: They notice when I've had a long day.
reaction: Noticing. I loved when he did that. A tiny 'rough one, huh?' That's all it took.
I want that again someday. With someone steady. With good cheese.

lines: If you could give one piece of advice about breakups to a friend, what would it be?
I'll write it on a sticky note.

choices.label: Be gentle with yourself.
reaction: Gentle. A beautiful word.
I wrote it on a sticky note and put it on my mirror.
Under 'drink water' and 'call Mom.' It's in good company.

choices.label: Let yourself feel it.
reaction: Feel it. That's the one I'm working on.
Not skipping to 'fine.' Sitting in the 'not fine' for a minute. It's uncomfortable.
But I think it's the way through.

dialogues.scene: Juniper holds out a small jar of pastel confetti.
lines: Look. It's the letter I never sent.
It's pretty now. I think that's the most poetic thing I've ever done. Do you want some? For luck?

choices.label: I'd love some.
reaction: Okay. Here, a pinch. It's a bit sticky. But it's lucky. I think.
It's made of things I needed to say. Now it's just shiny. That's a good transformation.

choices.label: Keep it for yourself.
reaction: That's what I thought you'd say. I'll keep it on my shelf.
A little jar of pastel feelings. It's like a snow globe, but sadder and prettier.

dialogues.scene: Juniper stands at the edge of the berry stand, looking at the sunset, and takes a long breath.
lines: Hey. I just realized I haven't thought about Rowan for three hours.
Three hours. That's the longest in a month. It felt kind of nice. And kind of weird. Like a quiet room.

choices.label: That's huge.
reaction: It is. I almost didn't notice.
I was too busy being mesmerized by a very good sunset. Okay, I noticed.
And then I thought of him for a second. But only a second. Progress.

choices.label: A quiet room is peaceful.
reaction: It really is. I used to think quiet meant empty. Today it felt like space.
Like a room with a window open. The breeze felt good. I might stay.
